aoi_name: Seih Al Hama, SW of Al Ain

baseline.note: velocities from the Landsat 8/9 OLI network (12 November scenes, 66 pairs); the Landsat 7 scenes (2000-11-27, 2001-11-30) are used only as a long-baseline check

speed_note: speeds are of the 1394 dune windows (480 m) with detected motion (58.3 % of 2391 valid); the other 997 move slower than their detection limit (median 0.45 m/yr) and are not in these statistics. Max detected 2.86 m/yr. uncertainty_myr = median calibrated 1-sigma per component.
wind_agreement_note: mean |heading - RDD| over detected windows, RDD 99.9 deg (MERRA-2 2000-2024). The wind regime is bimodal (RDP/DP 0.383): the field-median heading 28.8 deg is 28.8 deg from the northward (southerly-wind) mode and 71.1 deg from RDD; per-window median difference 74.1 deg.

published.their_value: 3.32 m average migration, peaking in 2019 (abstract; Sentinel-2, COSI-Corr, 2018-2020); time base not stated
published.note: Context only. The abstract gives '3.32 m' with no time base (per year, per month or per image pair), no area and no statistic, and the full text could not be read, so the number cannot be compared with a rate in m/yr (the two readings differ about 12-fold). It is also not confirmed that the thesis field ('Seih Al-Lahma' in its Arabic abstract) is this box. https://scholarworks.uaeu.ac.ae/all_theses/1432

second_dataset.their_value: HLS S30 (Sentinel-2, independent): field median 0.215 m/yr toward 340.1 deg; per-window correlation with Landsat r = 0.373 (E), 0.304 (N); its detection limit 0.852 m/yr, motion detected in 16.7 % of windows. HLS L30 (same Landsat instruments, not independent): 0.294 m/yr toward 20.4 deg, r = 0.691/0.68
second_dataset.our_value: Landsat pan 15 m over the same years: field median 0.412 m/yr toward 21.1 deg (S30 years); 0.403 m/yr toward 21.7 deg (L30 years)
second_dataset.note: The independent Sentinel-2 check agrees only weakly: speeds about half of Landsat's and headings 41.0 deg apart at field level, per-window r 0.373/0.304. At 30 m its detection limit (0.852 m/yr) is above most measured speeds, so it can confirm little; where Landsat speeds exceed twice the detection limit (140 windows) headings differ by a median 27.4 deg. HLS L30 agrees better (heading within 1.3 deg, speed 0.294 vs 0.403 m/yr) but uses the same Landsat instruments, so it only shows the result survives a different band, resolution and processing.

data_handling.display_only_frames: 11 Landsat 7 frames (2002-09-30, 2003-11-04, 2004-10-21, 2005-11-09, 2006-10-11, 2007-10-14, 2008-11-17, 2009-10-19, 2010-10-06, 2011-11-10, 2012-11-12; off-month: 2002-09-30, 2004-10-21, 2006-10-11, 2007-10-14, 2009-10-19, 2010-10-06) are shown on the timeline as images only, scan-line gaps left as no-data; they are not used in any number in this file (see frames/manifest.json observed_display_only).
data_handling.notes: 9 November candidate scenes rejected in notebook 01 (cloud/shadow/haze/coverage; listed in pipeline/outputs/seih_al_hama/scene_rejections.csv); Landsat 7 used only before the 31 May 2003 SLC failure. Clouds/shadows: Landsat QA_PIXEL bits 0-4 (dilated 1 px), HLS Fmask bits 1-3. Of 10100 tracking windows, 3065 lie outside the box and 4618 are mostly non-dune (vegetation, WorldCover, OSM, hand-drawn change areas); of the 2417 dune windows 1.08 % had too few valid pairs. Window-pair observations rejected: 3.32 % (weak match below the false-match threshold, displacement beyond the reliable range, network outliers).

limits: Speeds are slow: detected dune windows move a median 0.67 m/yr (10-90 %: 0.44-1.14, max 2.86), i.e. roughly 10-30 m in 25 years; 42 % of valid dune windows move below the detection limit (median 0.45 m/yr) and have no measured direction.

Reach years forecast the migration of dune forms (slip-face advance), not wind-blown sand crossing a road, which happens wherever a road borders loose sand, whatever the dunes do (see borders_free_sand in targets.geojson).

At these speeds the position of the sand edge matters as much as the speed: a 15 m pixel is about 20 years of motion at 0.7 m/yr, so reach years for targets near the sand carry an edge uncertainty of +-7.5 m plus the outline uncertainty of the target.
Most targets are not reached by 2050; targets flagged 'sand at edge now' already have migrating sand within that edge uncertainty.
The projection is advection along the measured 2013-2025 motion, assuming those conditions continue; it does not model dune deformation, merging, splitting or growth.
Vegetation, windbreaks, sand fences, levelling, construction and climate change alter the outcome.
Motion is measured in 480 m windows: it is the motion of the small dunes (spacing ~70-90 m) and sand sheets inside, not of a single dune body.
Only 21 large dunes (14-72 m high) are outlined, from NASADEM (February 2000) shifted to 2025; the small dunes that carry most of the motion are represented by the velocity grid, not by polygons.
The independent Sentinel-2 (HLS S30) check agrees only weakly; HLS L30 agrees better but uses the same Landsat instruments.
The published UAEU study is context only: its '3.32 m' has no stated time base, so no numeric comparison is made.
MERRA-2 wind is a ~0.5 x 0.625 deg reanalysis of hourly means; absolute drift potential is approximate and the regime is bimodal.
Farms are vegetated plots (HLS NDVI, last year) and built-up targets come from OpenStreetMap, where few buildings are mapped here; unmapped or abandoned plots are not targets.
Results are valid for this box and 2013-2025 only; nothing outside the box is assessed.

threat.reach_definition: Migrating dune sand (free sand inside a window whose dune-form migration is detected), carried along its measured heading at its measured speed, arrives at the edge of the target footprint (road: OSM centre line +- class half width incl. shoulders; farm: HLS vegetated outline; built-up: OSM outline).
excludes: wind-blown sand crossing or settling on a target
motion below the detection limit (no direction: never a hit)
dune deformation, merging, growth, levelling or stabilisation
threat.speeds: median = measured window speed v; fast = v + sigma; slow = v - sigma (sigma = calibrated per-component 1-sigma; 84th/16th percentiles of the speed)
threat.years: hit_year_min = floor(t0 + gap_lo / fast); hit_year_max = ceil(t0 + gap_hi / slow); gap = distance from the source pixel centre to the footprint along the heading minus 7.5 m, +-(7.5 m + outline uncertainty: roads/buildings 5 m, farms 15 m); t0 = 2025-11-08; earliest over all sand reaching the target; null if the fast case does not arrive by 2100

confirmation.rule: speed agrees if a check's field-median speed is within 15% of Landsat's over the same windows and years; heading agrees if the field-median headings differ by <= 20 deg (Landsat 7: per-window east and north correlations both >= 0.8). confirmed = the independent Sentinel-2 check (HLS S30) agrees; partly_confirmed = only the partly independent Landsat 7 long baseline agrees; not_confirmed = neither. HLS L30 uses the same Landsat 8/9 instruments and is shown for context only.

station_wind.role: Explanation of the difference between the measured dune heading and the MERRA-2 drift direction. MERRA-2 remains the primary wind figure; the station is evidence about the regional wind, not a measurement inside the dune field.
